runs.notes: A self-contained monochrome editorial field guide to the city after closing, with procedural canvas artwork, responsive layouts, and interactive field notes. No external assets or dependencies.

NOCTURNE — a monochrome single-page atlas of the night train. Twelve real sleeper services (1883 to today) presented as a split-flap departures board, a hand-drawn Beck-style route diagram, per-service night sequences, and four short elegies. Static HTML/CSS/JS with no dependencies and no external requests; the split-flap engine is DOM + Web Animations, board clacks are synthesized with the Web Audio API (off by default), the diagram is hand-authored SVG. Fully responsive, keyboard accessible, motion respects prefers-reduced-motion, works from file:// and GitHub Pages subpaths. Known limitations: timetable times are indicative rather than authoritative (stated on the page) and the diagram is deliberately schematic, not to scale.

Two Tones is a single-file, strictly greyscale interactive atlas of dithering. It renders procedural sphere, ramp and relief sources on canvas through four 1-bit methods (threshold, Bayer ordered, Floyd–Steinberg, Atkinson), and includes a live studio, a pointer-driven hero light, an orbit toggle, PNG export, scroll progress and reduced-motion support. It uses no external files, fonts or libraries. Limitation: verified with static checks and a stubbed-DOM run only, not in a real browser, so visual layout and motion are untested; browsers without :has() show the selected-state styling less clearly.

Single-page monochrome interactive experience 'GRAVITY': generative canvas particle fields, scroll-driven reveals, an interactive gravity-well demo, and a dark/light monochrome theme toggle. Static HTML/CSS/JS, no build step, relative paths. Known limitations: external Google Fonts dependency for typography; canvas animations disabled under prefers-reduced-motion.
